newsitem.title: UK: Woolwich shares seen opening around 370p.
newsitem.headline: Woolwich shares seen opening around 370p.

text.p: Shares in Britain's Woolwich Building Society were indicated sharply higher than expectations ahead of the market opening on Monday and the first of four share auctions to be held after the close tonight.
The shares were quoted at 373-1/2p at 0725 GMT compared with forecasts for the shares to open around the 320p level.
One head of market-making predicted the shares would debut at 350-370p, helped by takeover speculation and the lack of stock.

"No-one's got any stock yet because the first auction is not until the end of the day," he said. "Market-makers will open the stock very high to avoid selling them too cheaply, but then I expect the price to come rattling back before the auction tonight."
Another dealer agreed that at levels above 350p market-markers may be encouraged to sell.
In January, the advisers to the float BZW gave Woolwich an estimated market capitalisation of around three billion stg, putting a value of 200p on the shares.
The former building society is the third to demutualise after the Halifax and Alliance & Leicester and will be valued at more than five billion stg.
About 23 percent of Woolwich members opted to sell their free allocation of shares straight away and the first of four auctions will be held after the market closes.

Woolwich, like the Halifax and Alliance & Leicester, is expected to join the FTSE 100 index of top British companies, but not until September. Its entry into the leading index is likely to secure demand for the stock from tracker funds which aim to match the FTSE's performance.
